scope: Generic structural and search lessons; no circuit-specific node recipes or reference-area stopping rules
rules: Actual surviving physical standard-cell area decides acceptance; MFFC area is only screening potential.
Candidate error masks belong to one exact parent. Recompute responses after every accepted operation; do not add errors from different parents.
A high-area-gain near miss can justify a repair branch when excess errors are few and observable correction opportunities exist.
For compensation prioritize roots whose flip response repairs current wrong input indices with few new errors; single-output cuts can also compensate.
Preserve a feasible incumbent and at most four diverse active branches. Temporary area debt is useful only with a measured drop in error pressure.
Pure area-first constant selection can consume the error budget early. Compare error efficiency, area-rich alternatives and residual-function construction.
Use cached function definitions, but refresh area, signal survival, loops and error on the current parent before accepting.
A local rollout plateau is a tool result, not a proof of global convergence. Inspect unmeasured screened regions, wider cuts, near misses and recent weak decisions before choosing finish.
Counterfactual exchange should roll back an inefficient accepted action before trying a better replacement, rather than only adding more error-consuming operations.
Do not count cached truth-function scoring as an independent Monte Carlo propagation. Report both quantities and the actual gate evaluation work.
Training feasibility is not validation feasibility. Keep strict and overshoot results separate, and use a fresh final input stream after development selection.

An area-best candidate close to the training ER ceiling can fail independent validation. Maintain a lower-error frontier alongside high-gain near misses; an 80-90% training-error allowance is an exploration guide, never a replacement for final vector-ER acceptance.

Equal per-input vector-error masks on two candidates do not prove cancellation: different output bits can be wrong on the same input. Use overlap only for ranking and propagate every retained joint action.
A partial output-bit repair may leave vector ER unchanged while another output remains wrong. Preserve a few such repairs with positive bit-error recovery and test a bounded number of combinations.
Constant or alias primary outputs can still be compensation targets after their producer logic was deleted. Do not restrict repair to currently surviving multi-output windows.
Generated net and instance names can hide repeated physical structures. Deduplicate with a name-independent structural identity and preserve measured ancestors for a different action family.
Recompute responses when the parent changes, but reuse them across scans of the same immutable netlist. Root-response propagation counts and truth-function scores measure different work.
Many improving children do not necessarily improve the global frontier. Allocate more time only when feasible area at an error margin, or near-miss repair at a useful area, materially progresses.

Before abandoning a near-feasible compressed branch, preserve error-margin alternatives: a small measured area increase can recover substantial validation margin. Compare the measured Pareto frontier rather than only the lowest-area checkpoint.

When vector ER ties, preserve complementary partial repairs with large output-bit recovery alongside cheap input/constant alternatives. Expanding cheap choices must not crowd out the pair that can actually reduce vector ER.

A jointly rejected combination is measured evidence, not an empty failure. Use its actual area and vector ER to decide whether to authorize a repair branch; do not add scalar errors from individual candidates.

A globally profitable trajectory can begin with several small low-error replacements rather than spending most error allowance on the first maximum-area cut. Keep a budget-preserving branch and rescan for shared-logic bundles after its structure changes.

Joint materialized area gain can exceed the sum of single-node deletion gains when combined removals free shared upstream logic. Error-support similarity is a screening clue, not proof of signal-error cancellation.

Keep representative choices from distinct cost/error regimes visible to the global controller: area-rich, efficient, budget-preserving, repair and near-miss. Near-identical implementations of one target should not crowd out a useful small-error action.

Action definitions from the parent explain a child history, not executable choices on that child. Scan or use a bounded local rollout before selecting child candidate IDs; IDs bind both the immutable node and scan revision.

A budget-preserving local rollout should bound both each step error increment and total error pressure, refresh current-parent costs after each step, and return to global adjudication after a small declared number of steps. It is an option, not evidence that every circuit improves.

A replacement with zero or slightly negative individual area gain can be useful when several replacements together release a shared upstream cone. Screen by physical shared dependencies and actual retained inputs, then propagate only a few combinations; local potential is not measured area gain.

Already measured transitions explain existing children, not new actions. Revisit or scan the child instead of reapplying the same parent action. Compare actual rejected joint area/ER with bounded exploration limits and observed repair opportunities before expanding a near-miss branch.

A plateau from a small screened root region is not global convergence. A bounded broader or offset region scan can expose gains without growing the tree. Compare new area/error progress per tool-second; do not blindly extend an unchanged tree after a measured global-frontier plateau.

For a shared structural group, compare an area-rich alternative with prefixes of one error-input-guided chain. More operations can have much worse joint ER; summed scalar errors are not acceptance evidence. Keep the actual combined-trial cap fixed.

Deduplicating normalized physical structures before propagation can reduce Monte Carlo calls, but canonicalization and extra proxy work cost time. Reduced simulation count alone is not a measured wall-time speedup.

A duplicate first local choice is not evidence of a plateau. Try at most three already-screened ranked alternatives; identify stored physical circuits before propagation. Report duplicate skips separately from fresh simulations.

An area-best incumbent must not automatically displace a deliberately selected higher-area/lower-error branch from local refinement. Name the branch explicitly, retain the valid incumbent and impose a short step cap.

A repair that improves training and development ER can still worsen another input stream. Preserve failed checks and do not promote a near-boundary candidate or repair using only training margin; observed research test streams are not untouched confirmation.

Before paying for a near-miss repair, compare its area savings with the repair debt needed to remain better than the measured incumbent. Maximum permitted area debt is not a recommended default. A larger/lower-error branch is exploratory and needs an explicit measured recompression opportunity.

For a small overshoot, consider staged compensation: first meet formal training feasibility with modest area debt, then judge the marginal cost of extra error margin. A deep error-first target can undo far more area than the near miss saved.

Do not call a branch lower error merely because it is feasible; compare its measured error with the incumbent. Root flip evidence belongs to one exact parent, and a changed child needs its own response scan.

An offset region can be empty when the surviving circuit has fewer roots than the offset. Check measured total_roots; an empty scan is not evidence that new candidates were explored. Bounded region expansion can also fail to improve quality.
